deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is a fair copy in a clean secretary-like hand, with editorial bracket labels '((Blatt 17))' and '((Blatt 18; Heft))'. It is probably a copy prepared for the edition of Riemann's philosophical fragments, not Riemann's autograph.

Part 1 (Blatt 17): the programme statement of Riemann's 'Naturphilosophie' fragment. The aim is to trace the general laws of inanimate nature back to a common deeper ground. Two methodological norms are stated.
(1) Any action of one thing on another in space whose magnitude depends on distance must be propagated through space. This is a rejection of instantaneous action at a distance. Riemann claims Newton and Euler always held this view, and that it was pushed out of the scientific literature later, apparently through the combined influence of the Encyclopédistes and Kant. Other explanations of distance-dependence are not strictly impossible, but they lead to highly artificial and therefore improbable assumptions.
(2) All actions of ponderable bodies on ponderable bodies occur through a medium that fills space continuously ('stetig'). This is an ether or continuum hypothesis.
These norms are the starting point for Riemann's ether-based attempts to unify gravitation, light, electricity and magnetism. Those attempts are the 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' and the 'Gravitation und Licht' fragments, and they are related to his 1858 retarded-potential paper.

Part 2 (Blatt 18, 'Heft'): a rhetorical, quasi-religious passage in the Fechner context; the next page discusses Fechner's Nanna and Zend-Avesta. It says that certain ideas once powerful in human development are now reawakening in purer form. The life of nature, hitherto known only on the Earth's surface, is now immensely enlarged. What we took to be the seat of senseless, unconscious forces now appears as the workshop of the highest mental activity. This fulfils what 'our great poet' (presumably Goethe) foresaw as the goal of the inquiring mind.

Marginalia: a cross mark ('+' / '×'); 'Zweckmäßigkeit' in parentheses; and '4. (kann bis + abgekürzt werden) ??', i.e. this part may be shortened up to the '+' mark. These are editorial notes, apparently about abridging the passage for publication.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors to report.

Historical claim to flag: Newton's stance on action at a distance is debatable. He refused to feign hypotheses but privately (letter to Bentley, 1693) called unmediated action at a distance absurd. Euler did firmly advocate an ether. Attributing the decline of the propagation view to the Encyclopédistes and Kant is Riemann's own interpretive judgment.

results.what: Methodological norm: every distance-dependent interaction must be propagated through space (no instantaneous action at a distance).
results.modern_name: Locality / field-theoretic (contact-action) principle; finite propagation of interactions
results.usually_credited_to: Faraday and Maxwell (field concept, 1840s-1860s); in philosophy earlier Descartes, Euler and others

results.what: Norm: all ponderable-ponderable interactions are mediated by a continuous space-filling medium.
results.usually_credited_to: Euler, Huygens and 19th-century ether theorists; Riemann's version is published in his Naturphilosophie fragments (Werke, 1876)

results.what: Fechner-inspired panpsychist / Naturphilosophie rhetoric about nature as the workshop of the highest mental activity.

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely philosophical text. The Blatt 17 programme with its two norms is essentially the published opening of Riemann's 'Naturphilosophie' fragment in the Gesammelte Werke (ed. Weber and Dedekind, 1876). The Fechner-related passage belongs to his well-known engagement with Fechner. The page appears to be a later copy with editorial abridgment notes, and it contains no mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The hand is a neat copyist's or editor's fair copy, not Riemann's autograph; the '((Blatt 17))' and '((Blatt 18; Heft))' labels are editorial.
In 'nach welchem der Forschergeist hinstrebte' the word 'Forscher' (in 'Forschergeist') appears struck through in the image.

In 'welches bisher uns auf der Oberfläche der Erde sich ihm kund that', the word read as 'uns' may be 'nur' ('welches bisher nur auf der Oberfläche der Erde sich ihm kund that'), which fits the sense better.
The opening of Blatt 18 ('Sind Gesetze[?]') is uncertain in the image; it begins with a dash, suggesting a continuation from an earlier sheet.

Marginal notes: a pencil cross mark mid-page near norm 2, and to the right '(Zweckmäßigkeit)' above '4. (kann bis + abgekürzt werden) ??'. These are editorial notes about shortening, not part of the text.
Fragments of text from the facing page are visible at the right edge and are not part of this folio.
